output.reason: [ev-619c0cea3aa4] says only that the CA NameConstraints feature gate is promoted to Beta and is now enabled by default. Nothing in it says anything fails, is rejected or must be migrated, so behavior-change (review) with low severity is the right kind. The proposed statement, though, adds a detail the evidence doesn't give: that Certificate spec.nameConstraints is honoured. I've reworded the statement to stay within what the release note says.

correction.statement: In cert-manager 1.17.0 the CA NameConstraints feature gate is promoted to Beta and is now enabled by default. Environments that do not set the gate explicitly will have the CA NameConstraints feature active after the upgrade.

consequence.statement: If the NameConstraints feature gate is not set explicitly, the CA NameConstraints feature is enabled by default after upgrading to 1.17.0.
consequence.remediation: Check whether the CA NameConstraints feature should be on. If it should not, set NameConstraints=false explicitly in the feature gates.
